title: AGFM failure mode entry
description: Schema for a single entry in the AI Governance Failure Mode framework. Every entry must carry a plain-language example, and every regulatory mapping must carry a role scope naming who the obligation falls on.

id.description: Permanent identifier. Never reused, never renumbered, resolvable after deprecation.

plainTerms.description: One concrete situation in ordinary language. No acronyms, no framework references, no organization identifiable. An entry without this field is incomplete regardless of what else it contains.

entryStatus.description: 'full' carries the complete schema. 'open' is enumerated with a plain-language example and awaits contribution.

description.description: What the failure is, described generically.

variants.description: Sub-modes where the failure has materially distinct pathways.

indicators.description: Observable detection signals. The most operationally useful field in the schema.

rootCauses.description: Structural reasons the failure occurs. Non-blame-assigning by rule.

mitigations.description: Controls that address it. Tool-agnostic and vendor-neutral by rule.

mapping.description: Regulatory mappings. A mapping without a role scope is incomplete and does not publish.

framework.description: The instrument, e.g. 'EU AI Act', 'ISO/IEC 42001', 'SR 26-2'. Use 'No direct obligation' where a failure mode has no statutory hook.

provision.description: The specific article, clause, category or footnote, with any qualifying note.

role.description: Who the obligation falls on. This is the most common source of error in published crosswalks: citing a provider obligation to a deployer produces a compliance plan for a duty they do not hold.

status.description: 'live' = currently enforceable. 'future' = scheduled for a future date. 'stayed' = voluntary standard, or enforcement subject to a stay.

related.description: Adjacent failure mode identifiers. Builds the graph between entries.

reference.description: Public incident or enforcement reference where one exists. Left blank where none does, rather than invented.

tiers.description: Programme maturity tiers at which the failure typically surfaces.
